reviews.title: An inexpensive packaging hack that gives handmade products a beautiful, natural look.
reviews.body: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐I actually don't use these coffee filters for making coffee! I use them to package my handmade DIY shampoo bars and round soaps, and they work perfectly.They give my products a simple, natural, handcrafted look that my customers really like. To package them, I place the round soap or shampoo bar in the center of the filter and gently work my way around, pinching the filter a little at a time until it's wrapped snugly around the product. Then I place my round label on top to hold everything together. It creates a clean, professional presentation without spending a fortune on specialty packaging.Since I make and sell a lot of DIY products, keeping packaging costs down is important. These filters are an incredibly economical option, and you simply can't beat the price when you're packaging in larger quantities.They're well made, consistent in size, and have worked beautifully for my unconventional use. Sometimes the best packaging solutions come from thinking outside the box!**An inexpensive packaging hack that gives handmade products a beautiful, natural look.**

reviews.title: Exceptional Filters for the price.
reviews.body: Great quality filters.  Easy to use just drop into the filter basket or reusable filter basket and add the coffee grounds.  Keeps the mess of reusable mesh filters down, just loft out and rinse the filter or basket and you are ready to brew again.  The product is a good thickness and the stack weighs almost nothing (its paper).  The thickness is just right and does not affect brewing time, which actually allows the water to sit a little longer to absorb the coffee flavor.  If not overfilled with grounds, this will not allow the coffee grounds to leak over top and get into your coffee.  Great filters for the price!  Great for Craft use as well!

reviews.title: Perfect In So Many More Than Just Any Way.  Read On --
reviews.body: Brewing drip coffee is becoming a lost art.  Everybody seems to be OK with buying expensive cups at a street vendor or shop, or at least keeping their very own K machine to make their own personal special cuppa joe.  Might be the same folks who gripe about high costs.I'm not any of those, except I sometimes grumble about the costs of certain things.  These coffee filters are not one of those.  Truth be told, I don't drink coffee at all.  Don't tell anybody or I'll get bombarded with Keurig and Starbucks hate mail.We use coffee filters as flower and plant pot liners.  They get a filter, a bit of pea gravel, another filter, then soil goes in with the plant.  Keeps the soil where it should be, allows good drainage even when the pot sits in a cup or tray to retain the water.  Coffee filters are the perfect product for this.  Blasphemy?  Will Juan Valdez ride into town, looking for the cretin that doesn't drink coffee?  Will the coffee filter police show up at my door, 'splainin how there's some federal code that requires me to buy and filter coffee and the squeezins if I buy the filters?  Will our hero find his way out of that airless closet before we can rescue him?  Tune in next Monday for the conclusion of the series...These filters are inexpensive, available, probably do a spectacularly excellent job at keeping coffee grounds out of the cup or pot.  For us, a package lasts years, through hot and cold, rain or shine, snow, rain, ice, sun.  All to keep flowers and plants happy.  I could probably get used ones to work, and the house would smell like fresh-brewed coffee every morning.  The best part of waking up and all that.  Did I forget to mention I don't drink coffee?  Thought I'd said something.Net, these filters a great value for us.  Yes, we do highly recommend them.  Even for brewing coffee if you must.  :)
reviews.date: Reviewed in the United States on August 27, 2025
